newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals cheers S.Africa reserves rise, wary on rates.
newsitem.headline: Stals cheers S.Africa reserves rise, wary on rates.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Monday he was encouraged by a sharp rise in official gold and foreign exchange reserves last month but was cautious on the outlook for interest rates.
Asked whether the increase would help bring forward a rate cut, Stals told state radio:

"This very encouraging improvement in the foreign reserves over the past month is but one of the aspects that will influence it. We are guided very much by the rate of increase in domestic bank credit extension and the money suppy and inflationary trends in the domestic economy, so perhaps the emphasis is switching back agin to these domestic financial aggregates."

Total reserves of 11.76 billion in January, up from 10.31 billion in December, beat even the most optimistic forecasts. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a range of 10.5 to 11.5 billion with the consensus at 11.2 billion.
The January reserves were the highest since March 1996, with a jump in foreign assets of 1.83 billion rand more than offseting a 369 million rand decline in gold holdings.
